payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.

An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.

cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.

Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

payload.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 at 100, 500, 900 and 1300 metres along the pipe. Put this on the instrumentation track, not a pipeline leak-inspection track. No qualified inspection interval is available: the affected taps share one measurement path and lack independent corroboration. P2 belongs on the process/operating track; P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A need instrument checks, followed by the P4/P6 reading problems described below. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window, but this is not a leak exclusion.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 desk review to gateway-P7-0 and its eight taps; retain the separate-connection stations as contrasting evidence rather than treating eight alerts as independent witnesses.
2. Use the already reviewed OP-P2-EXTENDED-001 record to classify P2's broad rise as a matching operating transition, separate from the isolated P1/P3 changes.
3. Put P1-ST6-A, P3-ST7-A, P4-ST7-B, P6-ST3-A and P6-ST8-B on the instrument-review list; retain P1-ST7-B, P3-ST5-B and P4-ST8-A as observation gaps.
4. Seek independent physical pressure/flow confirmation for the P7 stations, outside gateway-P7-0, to distinguish a shared reading offset from real pressure loss. These are read-only review decisions, not dispatch or operating instructions.

Already checked
The specialists compared paired sensors, meaning two sensors at each station, and opened the operating and calibration records. P7's affected readings stepped down together around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording. They remained about 0.70-0.74 bar below typical normal pressure during seconds 130-150; bar is a pressure unit. Other P7 stations were near normal. MAINT-P7-GW-002 describes an approximately 0.75-bar downward conversion offset on exactly this shared connection. P2 instead rose about 0.36-0.39 bar in the recording, matching the logged positive transition during seconds 90-145; its latest five seconds returned near normal.

Why this decision
P1-ST6-A gradually rose, reaching about 0.89 bar above normal, while P3-ST7-A gradually fell to about 0.76 bar below normal; their paired B readings stayed near normal. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A had brief spikes; P6-ST8-B flatlined during the final 60 seconds. Missing readings affected P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B; P4-ST8-A had invalid readings. These observations justify checks, not confirmed hardware faults. Overall usable coverage was 99.18%, but the health review was partial.

What changes the decision
A sustained pressure loss independently measured outside P7's shared connection would raise integrity-review priority. A new P2 departure beyond the recorded transition would require a separate process assessment. The guidance distinguishes shared errors, operating changes and physical localization; incomplete operating logs and pressure patterns alone cannot settle the cause.

answer.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both A/B sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, respectively 100, 500, 900 and 1300 metres along the pipe. This is an instrumentation-review priority, not a pipeline leak-inspection interval: the affected readings lack independent corroboration outside that connection, so a qualified interval is withheld. Next, keep P2 on the process/operating track and P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A on the instrument track, followed by the P4/P6 reading problems below. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window; that does not exclude a concurrent leak.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 read-only review to gateway-P7-0 and its eight affected sensors. Use the already compared ST2 pair on gateway-P7-1 as contrasting evidence, not eight shared-path alerts as independent witnesses.
2. Use the opened OP-P2-EXTENDED-001 record to separate P2's matching positive transition from a new pressure-loss concern elsewhere.
3. Flag P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A for gradual drift, P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A for brief spikes, and P6-ST8-B for a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. Mark P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B as missing-data gaps and P4-ST8-A as invalid-reading gaps.
4. Seek independent physical pressure and flow confirmation at the affected P7 stations, outside gateway-P7-0, to distinguish actual pressure loss from a shared reading offset. Physical intervention requires separate verification and authorization.

Already checked
The specialists compared paired sensors, meaning two sensors at the same station, and opened operating and calibration records. P7's eight affected sensors stepped downward together around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording; before/after differences were about 0.73-0.75 bar, a pressure unit. Relative to typical normal pressure, ST1-A and ST3-A were respectively 0.71 and 0.72 bar lower during seconds 130-150, while ST2-A was 0.045 bar higher. These baseline differences are distinct from the within-recording step. The calibration record describes an approximately 0.75-bar downward conversion offset on exactly this connection.

Why this decision
P2's sixteen compared sensors rose about 0.36-0.39 bar, matching the logged positive transition during seconds 90-145. ST1-A and ST5-A were respectively 0.39 and 0.45 bar above normal during seconds 130-150; their final five-second readings were within 0.062 bar of normal. P1-ST6-A rose gradually to 0.89 bar above normal, whereas P3-ST7-A fell to 0.76 bar below normal; their B partners stayed near normal. Those disagreements support instrument checks, not confirmed hardware faults. Overall usable coverage was 99.18%, but the health review was partial and does not establish every sensor's reliability.

What changes the decision
Sustained pressure loss independently measured outside P7's shared connection would raise integrity-review priority. A new P2 departure beyond the recorded transition would require a separate process assessment. Shared-path guidance supports the present review priority, not a proven cause; incomplete operating logs leave competing causes unresolved.

competing_causes.text: P7 has measured pressure deficits, but the eight affected sensors all share gateway-P7-0 and therefore do not establish independent evidence of a physical leak. The compared ST2 pair on a separate connection lacks the downward step; ST2-A's recent pressure is slightly above normal, contrasting with the deficits at ST1-A and ST3-A. P3-ST7-A also declines without agreement from its paired B sensor. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window, and insufficient independent affected observers prevent a qualified inspection interval. Independent physical pressure and flow confirmation could distinguish a concurrent leak from a shared measurement offset.

The strongest instrumentation explanation is P7's synchronized downward offset, meaning readings shifted to a lower level, on one shared pressure-conversion connection. Its affected assets, approximate magnitude and timing match the calibration record, supporting connection review first without proving a hardware cause or identifying every connected sensor as faulty. Separately, P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A gradually diverge from stable paired references, P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show brief spikes, and P6-ST8-B becomes unchanging. The identified missing and invalid readings are observation gaps, not measured pressure losses. Independent references and read-only acquisition-status checks remain necessary to establish why these readings behave differently.

P2's sixteen paired readings rise across both data connections, with before/after changes of approximately 0.36-0.39 bar. Their positive sign, approximate magnitude and timing match the opened record describing an approximately 0.4-bar pressure-setting transition during seconds 90-145. As baseline-relative examples, ST1-A and ST5-A are approximately 0.39 and 0.45 bar above normal during seconds 130-150, then within 0.062 bar of normal in the final five seconds. This supports process attention rather than an instrument-fault label for the coherent rise. The association is not an exclusive causal explanation, does not explain P7's negative offset, and incomplete logs cannot exclude additional causes.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both A/B sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, respectively 100, 500, 900 and 1300 metres along the pipe. This is an instrumentation-review priority, not a pipeline leak-inspection interval: the affected readings lack independent corroboration outside that connection, so a qualified interval is withheld. Next, keep P2 on the process/operating track and P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A on the instrument track, followed by the P4/P6 reading problems below. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window; that does not exclude a concurrent leak.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 read-only review to gateway-P7-0 and its eight affected sensors. Use the already compared ST2 pair on gateway-P7-1 as contrasting evidence, not eight shared-path alerts as independent witnesses.
2. Use the opened OP-P2-EXTENDED-001 record to separate P2's matching positive transition from a new pressure-loss concern elsewhere.
3. Flag P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A for gradual drift, P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A for brief spikes, and P6-ST8-B for a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. Mark P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B as missing-data gaps and P4-ST8-A as invalid-reading gaps.
4. Seek independent physical pressure and flow confirmation at the affected P7 stations, outside gateway-P7-0, to distinguish actual pressure loss from a shared reading offset. Physical intervention requires separate verification and authorization.

Already checked
The specialists compared paired sensors, meaning two sensors at the same station, and opened operating and calibration records. P7's eight affected sensors stepped downward together around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording; before/after differences were about 0.73-0.75 bar, a pressure unit. Relative to typical normal pressure, ST1-A and ST3-A were respectively 0.71 and 0.72 bar lower during seconds 130-150, while ST2-A was 0.045 bar higher. These baseline differences are distinct from the within-recording step. The calibration record describes an approximately 0.75-bar downward conversion offset on exactly this connection.

Why this decision
P2's sixteen compared sensors rose about 0.36-0.39 bar, matching the logged positive transition during seconds 90-145. ST1-A and ST5-A were respectively 0.39 and 0.45 bar above normal during seconds 130-150; their final five-second readings were within 0.062 bar of normal. P1-ST6-A rose gradually to 0.89 bar above normal, whereas P3-ST7-A fell to 0.76 bar below normal; their B partners stayed near normal. Those disagreements support instrument checks, not confirmed hardware faults. Overall usable coverage was 99.18%, but the health review was partial and does not establish every sensor's reliability.

What changes the decision
Sustained pressure loss independently measured outside P7's shared connection would raise integrity-review priority. A new P2 departure beyond the recorded transition would require a separate process assessment. Shared-path guidance supports the present review priority, not a proven cause; incomplete operating logs leave competing causes unresolved.

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.

cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.

Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

Decision
Work first on pipeline P7's shared measurement connection, gateway-P7-0, serving paired A/B sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, at distances 100, 500, 900 and 1300 m along the pipe. This is an instrumentation-review priority, not a pipeline leak-inspection interval. No section qualifies for integrity inspection from these observations: independent support is inadequate. Next, keep P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A on individual-instrument review, P4/P6 on spike and stuck-reading checks, and P1/P3/P4 gaps on data-availability checks. P2 belongs on the operating-context track; P5 has no supported pressure-loss focus in the supplied summaries.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 desk review to gateway-P7-0 and its eight named taps; retain even-numbered stations on gateway-P7-1 as contrasting measurements, rather than treating eight taps as independent leak witnesses.
2. Separate P1-ST6-A/P3-ST7-A drift, P4-ST7-B/P6-ST3-A brief spikes, P6-ST8-B's stuck reading, and P1-ST7-B/P3-ST5-B/P4-ST8-A observation gaps from the shared P7 offset. Their paired references are not identified as suspect.
3. Use the already-opened P2 record to distinguish its recorded 90-145-second pressure-setting transition from a new loss; the supplied comparisons do not establish that historical P2 measurements matched it.
4. Seek independent pressure/flow confirmation outside gateway-P7-0 and confirmation of its actual calibration output to distinguish a reading shift from physical pressure loss.

Already checked
The focused 60-120-second comparison shows P7's eight affected taps falling 0.710-0.755 bar around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording; even-station changes range only from -0.014 to +0.027 bar. Bar is a pressure unit. The opened calibration record names this exact connection and approximately -0.75-bar offset. In the latest five seconds, affected taps remain 0.714-0.756 bar below verified-normal pressure, while even stations are approximately 0.010-0.061 bar above normal. This persistent deficit is not erased by small later changes.

Why this decision
P1-ST6-A gradually rises and P3-ST7-A gradually falls while their paired sensors remain stable; latest departures are respectively 3.772 bar above and 3.737 bar below normal. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show two brief spikes each, with approximately 2.6-bar jumps. P6-ST8-B becomes flat, unlike its changing partner. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 samples; P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid readings. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial.

What changes the decision
There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window across independent measurement paths. Sustained loss outside the shared P7 connection, worsening independent station pressures, or changes inconsistent with recorded operations would strengthen integrity review. The P2 record predicts a positive 0.4-bar transition, but current P2 readings are near normal. Guidance on independence, quality and operating context supports these distinctions, not a confirmed cause or operating authorization.

COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
instrumentation or telemetry (possible): P7's persistent offset—a reading shifted to a different level—follows the exact station membership of gateway-P7-0 and begins around the recorded calibration start. The focused comparison measures approximately 0.75-bar falls on its eight taps, while every other station, using the other shared data connection, remains near its previous level. Elsewhere, P3-ST7-A's large downward departure is contradicted by its stable same-station partner and develops as gradual drift, rather than an independently supported joint pressure loss. answer.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection serving both A/B sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, located 100, 500, 900 and 1300 m along the pipe. The strongest supported pattern belongs on the instrumentation track, not pipeline leak inspection. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent pressure-loss support is inadequate. Next, put P1/P3 on drift and missing-reading checks, P4/P6 on spike, invalid-reading and stuck-reading checks, and P2 on operating-context review. Keep P5 on lower-priority pressure/context review: reviewed P5-ST1-A and P5-ST5-A summaries are close to their normal reference, not a clearance of the whole pipe.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 read-only review to P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B. Keep even-numbered stations on gateway-P7-1 as comparison locations; eight taps sharing one connection are not eight independent witnesses.
2. Separate the individual reading problems listed below from P7's shared offset. Use the stable paired sensors as comparison references, not as identified faulty instruments.
3. Keep P2's logged positive pressure-setting transition separate from P7's negative shift. The opened record supplies operating context; the available comparisons do not establish a historical measurement match.
4. Seek independent P7 pressure and contemporaneous flow confirmation outside gateway-P7-0, plus its actual calibration output, to distinguish physical pressure loss from a shared reading shift.

Already checked
The focused comparison measures 0.710–0.755 bar falls on P7's eight affected taps around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording, versus changes of only -0.014 to +0.027 bar at even-numbered stations. Bar is a pressure unit. The calibration record names the same connection, start time and approximately -0.75-bar potential offset. Latest five-second readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A remain respectively 0.720 and 0.756 bar below the normal reference; P7-ST6-A is 0.061 bar above it. These reference-relative deficits are distinct from changes within the recording.

Why this decision
P1-ST6-A gradually rises and P3-ST7-A gradually falls while their paired sensors remain stable; latest departures are 3.772 bar above and 3.737 bar below the normal reference. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show brief spikes with approximately 2.6-bar jumps. P6-ST8-B becomes flat while its partner varies. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 samples; P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded invalid readings. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but the health review is partial and does not establish every instrument's reliability.

What changes the decision
There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window across independent measurement paths. Sustained independent pressure loss outside the shared P7 connection, or deterioration inconsistent with recorded operations, would strengthen integrity-review priority. Physical cause remains unresolved; independence and quality guidance support the review priority, not a hardware diagnosis or permission for intervention.

competing_causes.text: P7's persistent offset—a reading shifted to a different level—follows the exact station membership of gateway-P7-0 and begins around the recorded calibration start. The focused comparison measures approximately 0.75-bar falls on its eight taps, while every other station, using the other shared data connection, remains near its previous level. This supports reviewing the shared pressure-conversion path first, because agreement within one connection is not independent physical confirmation. Neither the record nor the timing proves a hardware fault or excludes a concurrent physical event. Independent pressure confirmation and the actual calibration output would distinguish those possibilities.

P7's pressure deficit is measured and persistent, but the affected stations all depend on one conversion path, with much quieter measurements at every other station. Elsewhere, P3-ST7-A's large downward departure is contradicted by its stable same-station partner and develops as gradual drift, rather than an independently supported joint pressure loss. These observations do not establish a leak or a qualified inspection interval, although pressure records alone cannot exclude one. Sustained independent pressure loss outside the suspect paths, together with independent pressure and flow confirmation, would strengthen the leak hypothesis and justify reassessing inspection priority.

The opened P2 record describes a pressure-setting transition between 90 and 145 seconds elapsed in the recording, with an expected positive change of about 0.4 bar. Its sign differs from P7's negative shift, so it does not explain that branch's observations. The executed historical comparisons do not include P2, preventing a measured match in sign, magnitude and timing; the reviewed latest P2 summaries are instead close to their normal reference. Operating-log coverage is incomplete and supplies no verified P5 action, so absent entries cannot exclude operating changes or leakage. Further incident-time operating evidence would be useful if an independent pressure change persists beyond the recorded transition.

follow_up_questions: Can an independent pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0 and contemporaneous flow evidence confirm whether P7's approximately 0.75-bar deficit is physical?
Does gateway-P7-0's actual calibration output confirm the recorded offset on P7-ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 A/B taps?
Can independent station references and acquisition-path checks distinguish drift at P1-ST6-A/P3-ST7-A and the stuck reading at P6-ST8-B from physical pressure behavior?

regional_assessments.text: On P7, both sensors at each odd-numbered station fall 0.710–0.755 bar around 90 seconds elapsed; even-numbered station changes remain between -0.014 and +0.027 bar. Latest five-second readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A are respectively 0.720 and 0.756 bar below their normal reference, while P7-ST6-A is 0.061 bar above it; these named summaries show a continuing deficit, not necessarily continuing decline. The calibration record names the affected shared connection and potential offset, making that measurement path the supported review focus. The eight affected taps share one failure domain, so their agreement does not supply independent physical confirmation or a qualified inspection interval. Independent pressure confirmation outside the connection and its actual calibration output would distinguish a common reading shift from physical loss.

P1-ST6-A gradually rises and P3-ST7-A gradually falls across the recording while their same-station partners remain stable; their latest departures are respectively 3.772 bar above and 3.737 bar below the normal reference. That disagreement supports individual reading-path checks rather than a joint leak-pattern label for P3. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show brief impulses with approximately 2.6-bar adjacent jumps, unlike their comparison partners; the profiles and extrema, not screening counts alone, support spike review. P6-ST8-B has an unchanging profile from the 90–135-second period onward and zero pressure range in the latest reviewed window, while P6-ST8-A continues varying. These are observed drift, spike and flatline patterns, not confirmed hardware faults; independent station references and read-only acquisition-path checks would distinguish reading problems from physical pressure behavior.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Work first on P7's gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection serving both A/B sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, located 100, 500, 900 and 1300 m along the pipe. The strongest supported pattern belongs on the instrumentation track, not pipeline leak inspection. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent pressure-loss support is inadequate. Next, put P1/P3 on drift and missing-reading checks, P4/P6 on spike, invalid-reading and stuck-reading checks, and P2 on operating-context review. Keep P5 on lower-priority pressure/context review: reviewed P5-ST1-A and P5-ST5-A summaries are close to their normal reference, not a clearance of the whole pipe.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 read-only review to P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B. Keep even-numbered stations on gateway-P7-1 as comparison locations; eight taps sharing one connection are not eight independent witnesses.
2. Separate the individual reading problems listed below from P7's shared offset. Use the stable paired sensors as comparison references, not as identified faulty instruments.
3. Keep P2's logged positive pressure-setting transition separate from P7's negative shift. The opened record supplies operating context; the available comparisons do not establish a historical measurement match.
4. Seek independent P7 pressure and contemporaneous flow confirmation outside gateway-P7-0, plus its actual calibration output, to distinguish physical pressure loss from a shared reading shift.

Already checked
The focused comparison measures 0.710–0.755 bar falls on P7's eight affected taps around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording, versus changes of only -0.014 to +0.027 bar at even-numbered stations. Bar is a pressure unit. The calibration record names the same connection, start time and approximately -0.75-bar potential offset. Latest five-second readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A remain respectively 0.720 and 0.756 bar below the normal reference; P7-ST6-A is 0.061 bar above it. These reference-relative deficits are distinct from changes within the recording.

Why this decision
P1-ST6-A gradually rises and P3-ST7-A gradually falls while their paired sensors remain stable; latest departures are 3.772 bar above and 3.737 bar below the normal reference. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show brief spikes with approximately 2.6-bar jumps. P6-ST8-B becomes flat while its partner varies. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 samples; P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded invalid readings. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but the health review is partial and does not establish every instrument's reliability.

What changes the decision
There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window across independent measurement paths. Sustained independent pressure loss outside the shared P7 connection, or deterioration inconsistent with recorded operations, would strengthen integrity-review priority. Physical cause remains unresolved; independence and quality guidance support the review priority, not a hardware diagnosis or permission for intervention.

answer.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection serving both A/B sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, located 100, 500, 900 and 1300 m along the pipe. The strongest supported pattern belongs on the instrumentation track, not pipeline leak inspection. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent pressure-loss support is inadequate. Next, put P1/P3 on drift and missing-reading checks, P4/P6 on spike, invalid-reading and stuck-reading checks, and P2 on operating-context review. Keep P5 on lower-priority pressure/context review: reviewed P5-ST1-A and P5-ST5-A summaries are close to their normal reference, not a clearance of the whole pipe.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 read-only review to P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B. Keep even-numbered stations on gateway-P7-1 as comparison locations; eight taps sharing one connection are not eight independent witnesses.
2. Separate the individual reading problems listed below from P7's shared offset. Use the stable paired sensors as comparison references, not as identified faulty instruments.
3. Keep P2's logged positive pressure-setting transition separate from P7's negative shift. The opened record supplies operating context; the available comparisons do not establish a historical measurement match.
4. Seek independent P7 pressure and contemporaneous flow confirmation outside gateway-P7-0, plus its actual calibration output, to distinguish physical pressure loss from a shared reading shift.

Already checked
The focused comparison measures 0.710–0.755 bar falls on P7's eight affected taps around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording, versus changes of only -0.014 to +0.027 bar at even-numbered stations. Bar is a pressure unit. The calibration record names the same connection, start time and approximately -0.75-bar potential offset. Latest five-second readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A remain respectively 0.720 and 0.756 bar below the normal reference; P7-ST6-A is 0.061 bar above it. These reference-relative deficits are distinct from changes within the recording.

Why this decision
P1-ST6-A gradually rises and P3-ST7-A gradually falls while their paired sensors remain stable; latest departures are 3.772 bar above and 3.737 bar below the normal reference. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show brief spikes with approximately 2.6-bar jumps. P6-ST8-B becomes flat while its partner varies. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 samples; P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded invalid readings. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but the health review is partial and does not establish every instrument's reliability.

What changes the decision
There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window across independent measurement paths. Sustained independent pressure loss outside the shared P7 connection, or deterioration inconsistent with recorded operations, would strengthen integrity-review priority. Physical cause remains unresolved; independence and quality guidance support the review priority, not a hardware diagnosis or permission for intervention.

competing_causes.text: P7's persistent offset—a reading shifted to a different level—follows the exact station membership of gateway-P7-0 and begins around the recorded calibration start. The focused comparison measures approximately 0.75-bar falls on its eight taps, while every other station, using the other shared data connection, remains near its previous level. This supports reviewing the shared pressure-conversion path first, because agreement within one connection is not independent physical confirmation. Neither the record nor the timing proves a hardware fault or excludes a concurrent physical event. Independent pressure confirmation and the actual calibration output would distinguish those possibilities.

P7's pressure deficit is measured and persistent, but the affected stations all depend on one conversion path, with much quieter measurements at every other station. Elsewhere, P3-ST7-A's large downward departure is contradicted by its stable same-station partner and develops as gradual drift, rather than an independently supported joint pressure loss. These observations do not establish a leak or a qualified inspection interval, although pressure records alone cannot exclude one. Sustained independent pressure loss outside the suspect paths, together with independent pressure and flow confirmation, would strengthen the leak hypothesis and justify reassessing inspection priority.

The opened P2 record describes a pressure-setting transition between 90 and 145 seconds elapsed in the recording, with an expected positive change of about 0.4 bar. Its sign differs from P7's negative shift, so it does not explain that branch's observations. The executed historical comparisons do not include P2, preventing a measured match in sign, magnitude and timing; the reviewed latest P2 summaries are instead close to their normal reference. Operating-log coverage is incomplete and supplies no verified P5 action, so absent entries cannot exclude operating changes or leakage. Further incident-time operating evidence would be useful if an independent pressure change persists beyond the recorded transition.

regional_assessments.text: On P7, both sensors at each odd-numbered station fall 0.710–0.755 bar around 90 seconds elapsed; even-numbered station changes remain between -0.014 and +0.027 bar. Latest five-second readings at P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A are respectively 0.720 and 0.756 bar below their normal reference, while P7-ST6-A is 0.061 bar above it; these named summaries show a continuing deficit, not necessarily continuing decline. The calibration record names the affected shared connection and potential offset, making that measurement path the supported review focus. The eight affected taps share one failure domain, so their agreement does not supply independent physical confirmation or a qualified inspection interval. Independent pressure confirmation outside the connection and its actual calibration output would distinguish a common reading shift from physical loss.

P1-ST6-A gradually rises and P3-ST7-A gradually falls across the recording while their same-station partners remain stable; their latest departures are respectively 3.772 bar above and 3.737 bar below the normal reference. That disagreement supports individual reading-path checks rather than a joint leak-pattern label for P3. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A show brief impulses with approximately 2.6-bar adjacent jumps, unlike their comparison partners; the profiles and extrema, not screening counts alone, support spike review. P6-ST8-B has an unchanging profile from the 90–135-second period onward and zero pressure range in the latest reviewed window, while P6-ST8-A continues varying. These are observed drift, spike and flatline patterns, not confirmed hardware faults; independent station references and read-only acquisition-path checks would distinguish reading problems from physical pressure behavior.
